news.Title: Can GFS' Manufacturing Expansion Boost Its Future Growth Prospects?
news.Content:
GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc . GFS has been selected to operate two new semiconductor manufacturing facilities at its Malta, New York, campus under a U.S.-Japan investment initiative worth up to $21 billion. The expansion will increase the company's U.S. production capacity and support demand for chips used in automotive, industrial, communications and data center applications.

Under the project, GlobalFoundries will use Japan's initial investment of around $10 billion to build a new semiconductor manufacturing plant, which is expected to begin operations in 2029. An additional investment of approximately $10 billion could fund a second facility. Each plant is expected to add around 900,000 300mm wafers of annual production capacity. The project is expected to create approximately 27,000 construction and related jobs, along with more than 1,000 skilled manufacturing positions.

Separately, the company will reallocate $955 million from its existing U.S. government award to invest in silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and advanced packaging at its New York and Vermont facilities. These technologies are expected to support growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI), cloud data centers and high-speed communications.

The investment could strengthen GlobalFoundries' position in the U.S. semiconductor market, support key customers such as Renesas, Apple, Cirrus Logic and General Motors, and enhance its role in the global semiconductor supply chain.

GlobalFoundries' Peers

United Microelectronics Corporation UMC provides semiconductor foundry services for chips used in communications, automotive, consumer electronics and industrial applications. The company specializes in mature and specialty process technologies, including solutions for display drivers, power management and connectivity. UMC focuses on manufacturing reliability, process efficiency and long-term customer relationships to support demand for chips across a wide range of electronic devices.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM manufactures advanced semiconductors for leading global technology companies, supporting applications such as AI, high-performance computing and mobile devices. Its advanced process technologies help produce powerful, energy-efficient chips for smartphones, AI accelerators and high-performance computing systems. TSMC provides advanced packaging technologies that help improve chip performance and meet the growing computing demands of next-generation applications.

Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL develops semiconductor solutions for data infrastructure, including AI systems, cloud computing and data centers. Its portfolio includes networking chips, optical connectivity solutions and custom silicon designed to support high-speed data transfer and efficient computing. As AI workloads increase the need for faster connectivity and greater data processing capacity, Marvell is focusing on technologies that help cloud providers and enterprise customers build scalable, high-performance infrastructure.

news.Title: NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 27, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $4.14 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +33.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $3.77 billion, up 18.8% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.47% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for NXP?

For NXP, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.27%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that NXP will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that NXP would post earnings of $3.54 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.61, delivering a surprise of +1.98%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

NXP doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Title: Google’s Next AI Chip Is Running Late. Why Marvell May Be Fine
news.Content:
Google's next TPU chip is reportedly facing delays. Still, GF Securities believes Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL ) remains well-positioned in Google's chip supply chain over the medium and long term. How should investors interpret the delay for Marvell's stock? If you're weighing MRVL's AI growth potential against short-term uncertainty, these 11 AI stocks are worth a closer look, with Marvell securing the No. 7 spot.

A Delay, Not a Demand Problem

GF Securities says one part of Google's TPU v9 design has slipped by about three weeks, likely due to a redesign. That small delay pushes the timeline back by about a quarter. Tape-out is now scheduled for January 2027, mass production for the second quarter of 2027, and shipments for the first quarter of 2028. Packaging substrate yields are a key obstacle, at just 45% to 50%. However, GF Securities believes it has identified the underlying causes of the problem.

The firm does not see demand as a concern. GF analyst Jeff Pu highlights strong demand for Google's TPUs from both Google itself and external customers, including Anthropic. GF suggests that this external demand may be one reason Gemini 4 is arriving later than expected, as a significant share of Google's TPU v7 went to outside customers in the first half of 2026. The firm identifies MediaTek, rather than Marvell, as facing short-term headwinds. Because the note offers no specific details about Marvell's role in the supply chain, any benefit from the situation appears indirect. However, Jeff Pu's own posts associate v9 with MediaTek, whereas Marvell's potential Google opportunity involves later-generation chips and remains uncertain. As a result, the delay is unlikely to have much direct impact on Marvell. The delay may not change MRVL's short-term outlook, but its AI potential keeps it on investors' radar. Explore our list of 10 AI stocks that could skyrocket, featuring Marvell .

Does Google's Delay Move Marvell's Stock?

At 63x forward earnings, Marvell trades at a 66% premium to its five-year average P/E of 38.02x. So the stock does not look undervalued. Using estimates for the next fiscal year, the multiple comes down to approximately 37x to 40x, near the average, although the two measures use different bases. Investors are paying up for strong earnings growth. EPS is projected to increase 48.59% this fiscal year and 72.58% the next year, with growth accelerating rather than easing.

But that valuation leaves little room for delays. Investors are paying upfront for growth that must arrive on schedule. At its recent investor day, management set long-term targets of roughly $80 billion in revenue and $30 in non-GAAP EPS by calendar year 2030, according to Morningstar. The current premium reflects expectations for that growth. However, Marvell does not seem to generate meaningful revenue from TPU v9, which GF's analyst attributes to MediaTek. As a result, the delay has only a limited, indirect impact on the stock and is not, by itself, a reason to buy.

Story Continues

In my view, the premium is justified only if Marvell delivers the expected growth on time. If that still doesn't impress you, you can compare it with 9 other stocks in our list of Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 .

Hedge fund ownership of Marvell grew from 79 funds at the end of Q1 2026 to 96 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest accounted for 3.21% of float as of September 30, 2026.

GF's comments indicate that Marvell's longer-term position in Google's chip supply chain remains intact. But the note does not specify Marvell's role, while rising hedge fund ownership signals broader institutional participation. Still, a 63x multiple on this year's earnings leaves little room for delays. The company needs to deliver on the expected timeline to support its valuation.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MRVL as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than MRVL and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Meta Platforms, Lam Research, Texas Instruments, Tesla, Netflix, Procter & Gamble and GE Aerospace
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 20, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Meta Platforms META, Lam Research LRCX, Texas Instruments TXN, Tesla TSLA, Netflix NFLX, Procter & Gamble PG and GE Aerospace GE.

Here are highlights from Monday's Analyst Blog:

Q3 Earnings Reports Gear Up: Global Week Ahead

What happens across this Global Week Ahead?

·        Q3 earnings season is shifting up a gear in the U.S., and

·        Mainland China is about to deliver a deluge of macro data

·        Giving febrile markets plenty more to ponder after the latest bouts of volatility in bonds and AI stocks

Elsewhere:

·        Central bankers in Indonesia and Turkey have been given headaches by global index provider MSCI, while

·        Voters in Brazil gear up to choose their next president

Next are Reuters' five world market themes, re-ordered for equity traders—

(1) Q3 Earnings Season Is Here

U.S. earnings season picks up in the coming days, with investors focused on Meta Platforms and other AI-focused companies as technology shares wobble.

Meta, due on Wednesday, is one of several hyper-scalers whose massive spending on AI data centers and infrastructure has been a big driver of investment.

With concerns mounting over financing for the AI buildout, investors want more detail on expected returns from those huge outlays.

Reports from semiconductor companies Lam Research and Texas Instruments will offer another view of the AI boom, as will results from Elon Musk's Tesla .

Other high-profile results in the coming days include Netflix , Procter & Gamble and GE Aerospace .

S&P500 earnings are expected to have climbed more than +30% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES, continuing a robust year for corporate profits.

(2) Stock & Bond Returns Correlation a Focus

For months, as energy and food prices surged amid the Iran war, bonds lost their shock-absorber status as investors jacked up estimates of how high interest rates might need to go.

Add near-chronic concern ‌about developed-world governments' finances, and bonds seemed to offer little safe-haven comfort while still struggling to rival super-charged equities.

The correlation between stocks and bond yields has now turned positive for Europe and the U.S., meaning yields are more likely to fall when stocks fall.

It had been overwhelmingly negative this year, with yields rising as stocks fell, undermining bonds' traditional role as a haven during equity selloffs.

Story Continues

This relationship fluctuates, but this year, the correlation of U.S. stocks and bond yields in March hit its most negative since at least the 1990s, while for European assets, it reached its most negative on record in September.

(3) MSCI Proposed Stripping Indonesia of EM Status. Turkey Put on Notice, Too

Central bankers in Indonesia and Turkey already have plenty on their plates.

Now they have an MSCI headache, too.

Indonesia's central bank meets on Wednesday, while Turkish policymakers gather on Thursday, against a backdrop of high energy prices, rising borrowing costs, AI-driven market disruption and geopolitical uncertainty.

MSCI has proposed stripping Indonesia of its emerging-market (EM) status and removing it from a suite of indexes, a move that risks triggering heavy outflows and raising pressure on policymakers to hike from 5.75% rather than hold.

MSCI has also put Turkey on notice, warning of a potential downgrade if market reforms fall short by mid-2027, another complication for policymakers expected to keep cutting rates from 37%.

(4) The Week Starts with a Mainland China Macro Data Deluge

A health check on the Chinese economy is due on Monday, with third-quarter GDP alongside September retail sales, industrial output and fixed-asset investment data.

The latest loan prime rate follows on Tuesday and is expected to stay put after more than a year on hold.

Strong global demand for semiconductors, clean technology and other manufactured goods has kept China's economy ticking, even as domestic demand remains patchy and higher energy costs bite.

Exports have held up despite China's delicate trade balancing act with the U.S. and E.U.

The latest trade figures showed Chinese exports surging well beyond analysts' estimates, putting the country on track for another $1 trillion trade surplus this year after crossing the threshold for the first time in 2025.

The flip side: the export boom could add to trade tensions with major partners.

(4) Brazil's Presidential Runoff Happens on October 25th. Campaigning Underway

Brazil's October 25th presidential runoff is keeping markets on edge after Flávio Bolsonaro's surprise first-round lead sent stocks up 7.7% and the real almost 4% higher.

A new Quaest poll puts Bolsonaro on 46% versus Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 44%, a technical tie.

Investors are betting a Bolsonaro win would bring tighter fiscal policy, but much may already be priced in. His choice of economic team and signs of credible reform could fuel further gains.

A Lula comeback, meanwhile, could put that rally into reverse, with the real, longer-dated bonds and state-controlled companies among the most exposed. A more conservative Congress, though, could limit how far Lula could shift policy.

news.Title: Nasdaq Futures Slip as AI Stocks Resume Slide, Oil Jumps; SpaceX Earnings on Tap
news.Content:
December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are down -0.55% this morning as chipmakers and other AI-related stocks came under renewed selling pressure.

Sentiment toward the AI trade weakened again on Tuesday after the disastrous debut of a South Korean data center company reignited doubts about the sustainability of the AI spending boom. AI infrastructure provider Elice cratered -32% in Seoul, marking the worst trading debut for a sizable company in the country. The disappointing debut triggered a fresh wave of selling in AI-related stocks across the globe. Micron Technology (MU), Marvell Technology (MRVL), and Sandisk (SNDK) each fell more than -2% in U.S. pre-market trading.

More News from Barchart

No 'Example Anywhere on the Planet': Billionaire Kevin O'Leary's Utah Data Center Could Use Enough Electricity to Power 16 Million People

Dear GE Aerospace Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 20

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 20

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Further dampening risk appetite, the price of WTI crude climbed more than +2% on Tuesday as traders weighed lingering Middle East supply risks. Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said on Monday that Tehran has "no choice" but to establish control over the Strait of Hormuz to protect its security. Traders took the remarks as a signal that Iran could intensify attacks on tankers passing through the waterway, prompting them to price in a higher geopolitical risk premium.

Investors are now awaiting U.S. housing market data and a slew of corporate earnings reports, with a particular focus on SpaceX's results.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's main stock indexes ended mostly higher, buoyed by a rebound in chipmakers. Chip and AI infrastructure stocks climbed, with Western Digital (WDC) rising over +6% to lead gainers in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 and Sandisk (SNDK) gaining more than +5%. Also, Amazon.com (AMZN) advanced nearly +5% and was the top percentage gainer in the Dow after Morgan Stanley named the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant a top pick and raised its price target on the stock to $350 from $335. In addition, Datadog (DDOG) surged more than +5% after Bernstein upgraded the stock to Outperform from Market Perform with a price target of $350. On the bearish side, NRG Energy (NRG) slid over -4% after Jefferies and Seaport Research lowered their price targets on the stock.

Story Continues

"The final three months of the year have historically been favorable for stocks. Although there is no guarantee these historical patterns will continue in 2026, strong corporate profit growth and resilient economic activity could support further gains through year-end," said Brock Weimer at Edward Jones.

Third-quarter corporate earnings season is gathering pace, with investors awaiting results from high-profile companies today, including SpaceX (SPCX), GE Aerospace (GE), Netflix (NFLX), RTX Corp. (RTX), Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), and 3M Company (MMM). SpaceX's earnings report, due after the closing bell, will draw particular attention. Investors will be keen to hear updates from CEO Elon Musk on the ambitious goals he laid out during the previous earnings call in August, including plans to launch data centers in space in 2027 and achieve $1 trillion in revenue by 2030. According to Bloomberg Intelligence, S&P 500 companies are expected to post an average +25% jump in third-quarter earnings from a year earlier.

On the economic front, investors will focus on U.S. building permits (preliminary) and housing starts data, set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists expect September building permits to total 1.390 million and housing starts to total 1.300 million, compared with the prior month's figures of 1.403 million and 1.275 million, respectively.

The National Association of Realtors' pending home sales data will also be released today. Economists project pending home sales to fall -0.7% m/m in September following a +0.3% m/m rise in August.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in an 82.8% probability of no rate change and a 17.2% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the conclusion of the Fed's October meeting.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 5.13%, down -0.18%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is down -0.97% this morning as a fresh wave of selling in AI-related stocks across the globe weighed on sentiment. Rising oil prices further dampened investors' appetite for risk. Technology and bank stocks led the declines on Tuesday. Investors also digested a raft of regional economic data. The ZEW Economic Institute reported on Tuesday that German investor sentiment weakened in October for the first time in six months. Separately, data showed that U.K. wage growth picked up slightly in the three months through August, while the unemployment rate unexpectedly fell, strengthening expectations that the Bank of England will raise its key interest rate next month. In addition, data showed that the Eurozone's current account surplus narrowed in August to its lowest level since January 2023. Meanwhile, Eurozone government bond yields fell on Tuesday as renewed concerns about the AI trade prompted investors to seek refuge in safe-haven assets. In corporate news, ABB (ABB.S.DX) slumped over -5% even as the Swiss engineering group boosted its full-year guidance.

U.K. Average Earnings ex Bonus, U.K. Unemployment Rate, Germany's ZEW Economic Sentiment Index, Eurozone's ZEW Economic Sentiment Index, and Eurozone's Current Account data were released today.

U.K. Average Earnings ex Bonus rose +3.7% in the three months to August, stronger than expectations of +3.6%.

The U.K. Unemployment Rate was 4.7% in the three months to August, stronger than expectations of no change at 4.9%.

The German October ZEW Economic Sentiment Index came in at 28.1, weaker than expectations of 30.2.

The Eurozone October ZEW Economic Sentiment Index arrived at 18.5, weaker than expectations of 23.6.

Eurozone's August Current Account came in at 8.7 billion euros, weaker than expectations of 29.2 billion euros.

Asian stock markets today closed mixed. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed up +0.12%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -1.30%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed slightly higher today, supported by gains in the technology sector. Tech stocks advanced on Tuesday, bucking a slump among their regional peers. However, declines in financial and gold-related stocks capped the benchmark's gains. Meanwhile, China left its benchmark lending rates unchanged for a 17th consecutive month on Tuesday, in line with expectations, as authorities increasingly rely on fiscal expansion to support economic growth. The one-year loan prime rate was held steady at 3.00%, while the five-year LPR remained at 3.50%, according to the People's Bank of China. The decision came after China's central bank signaled plans to continue overhauling the country's monetary policy framework, placing greater emphasis on shorter-term interest rates to better steer markets. PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said on Monday that companies with stronger financial positions could eventually be permitted to choose between the interbank overnight repo rate and LPRs as the reference rate for floating-rate loans. "The potential shift to an overnight policy rate could effectively amount to a policy rate cut, depending on the level at which the new rate is set," according to Goldman Sachs' Xinquan Chen. Elsewhere, two Chinese technology companies launched share offerings in Hong Kong aimed at raising a combined $1.5 billion, testing investor demand amid ongoing concerns about the AI trade.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed lower today, failing to follow Wall Street's overnight rally. Technology stocks were among the biggest losers on Tuesday as sentiment toward the AI trade remained jittery. Tech investor SoftBank Group sank over -6%, making it the biggest drag on the Nikkei. The drop came after the company's credit risk, as measured by its credit-default swaps, climbed to the highest level in almost four years amid mounting concerns over AI-related financing and a possible large acquisition. Losses in financial and industrial stocks also weighed on the benchmark. Meanwhile, Japanese government bond yields fell on Tuesday after an auction of 20-year bonds attracted record demand, signaling that elevated yields are beginning to draw domestic investors back into the market. Elsewhere, Reuters reported on Tuesday that the Bank of Japan is likely to leave interest rates unchanged this month but could raise its inflation forecast for the next fiscal year, as rising oil prices keep price pressures elevated for longer than previously expected. Investor focus this week is on Japan's national core CPI for September. Market participants will also closely watch Japan's preliminary October PMIs and September trade figures. In addition, the BOJ will publish its semiannual Financial System Report at the end of the week. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +3.04% at 32.18.

Pre-Market U.S. Stock Movers

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks slid in pre-market trading. Micron Technology (MU), Marvell Technology (MRVL), and Sandisk (SNDK) each fell more than -2%.

Apple (AAPL) slipped nearly -1% in pre-market trading after Loop Capital downgraded the stock to Hold from Buy with a price target of $330.

Steel Dynamics (STLD) slid about -5% in pre-market trading after the steelmaker posted weaker-than-expected Q3 results.

Solstice Advanced Materials (SOLS) rose over +3% in pre-market trading after the Financial Times reported that activist investor Starboard Value had built a stake in the company.

Energy stocks advanced in pre-market trading as oil prices rose, with APA Corp. (APA) and Chevron (CVX) gaining more than +1%.

news.Title: Is Marvell Technology a Millionaire-Maker Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) is deeply involved in artificial intelligence infrastructure, with its optical chips, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), data storage controllers, and CXL memory products. This broad portfolio of products explains why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said back in June that he expects Marvell Technology to be the next $1 trillion company.

Given its current market cap of around $215 million, that prediction implies a nearly 5x return from current levels, a gain that could help mint many new millionaires, and the fundamentals certainly look promising. Here's what investors should know.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Marvell's long-term deal with Alphabet gives it a massive backlog

Marvell Technology is already doing well. In its fiscal 2027 second quarter, which ended Aug. 1, the company delivered 37% year-over-year revenue growth, with "AI-related bookings remain[ing] exceptionally robust," according to Marvell Technology CEO Matt Murphy. He also expects AI revenue to accelerate further in fiscal 2027, prompting the company to raise its guidance for fiscal 2027 and 2028.

Moreover, after that quarter ended (but before its report came out), the company announced a big expansion of its AI chip deal with Alphabet . It amounts to $120 billion over roughly six and a half years, and that business arrangement starts in Marvell's fiscal 2029.

Marvell Technology will continue to strengthen its market position in the meantime, and if it can land big deals like that with other tech giants, it could see an extended rally. Marvell Technology generated $2.74 billion in sales in its fiscal Q2 while boosting net profit margins, and its guidance for the upcoming quarter implies 15% sequential revenue growth at the midpoint.

A high valuation is the price of entry

Although Marvell Technology has several attractive catalysts ahead of it, the stock isn't cheap. It trades at a forward P/E ratio of 62. Other chipmakers such as Broadcom and Nvidia offer cheaper valuations and solid growth prospects. Furthermore, those two companies are exhibiting higher revenue growth rates than Marvell Technology.

While Nvidia and Broadcom look more attractive if you only consider next year, Marvell Technology may be the better choice when considered over a five-year time horizon. Its big deal with Alphabet will contribute roughly $5 billion per quarter in sales once it starts, and that's almost two times Marvell Technology's Q2 FY27 revenue.

Story Continues

Marvell Technology is still of a size where a single new contract of that magnitude can change the investment thesis in the stock overnight. Nvidia is on its way to more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue, so it would need multiple large contracts to sustain meaningful growth. Marvell Technology is well-positioned to gain market share as optical chips and ASICs gain traction. A few more major contracts could spark a rally that lifts its market cap closer to Jensen Huang's $1 trillion prediction.

news.Title: Sandisk (SNDK) at 6 Times Forward Earnings, Is a Peak Already Priced In?
news.Content:
Memory chip stocks came under heavy selling last week after China's CXMT claimed a chip technology breakthrough. Bloomberg reported that traders fear the move will add Chinese memory supply and set off a price war.

That fear lands on a company whose recent profit jump came mostly from higher prices. Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), the flash storage maker Western Digital spun off in early 2025, got about two-thirds of its fiscal fourth-quarter revenue growth from pricing rather than volume. Yet the stock now trades near 6 times estimated earnings for the fiscal year under way, well below its sector, and long-term contracts cover a large share of its output.

So is the market right to price in a peak? The facts suggest it is pricing a sharper fall in profit than Sandisk's own contracts and guidance imply, at least for the next year or so.

Sandisk makes NAND flash storage, including solid state drives, memory cards and USB drives. It sells them to data centers, makers of edge devices, and consumers. Revenue reached $8.97 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, up 51% from the quarter before. If you're looking for undervalued AI stocks, check out 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now .

Higher Prices Drove the Latest Jump

Gross margin hit 84.6% in the fiscal fourth quarter, compared with 26.2% a year earlier, which shows how much pricing mattered. The risk is that so much of that margin came from price rather than volume.

Data centers are the newer piece of the business. Datacenter revenue reached nearly $3 billion in the quarter, more than double the quarter before. CEO David Goeckeler said Sandisk now counts data centers as a key growth pillar, with deeper customer partnerships.

Contracts Now Cover Half of Next Year's Output

Sandisk has tried to lock in some of those gains. At its investor day, the company said it had signed new business model agreements with eight customers. They cover about half of its output, measured in bits, in fiscal 2027 and about two-thirds in fiscal 2028. Sandisk described them as enforceable contracts with minimum financial guarantees.

That is the best answer to the price-war worry, but not a full one. A contract floor does nothing for prices on the rest of the output, and the investor-day release does not say how high the floors are. Guidance points to slower profit growth. Sandisk expects adjusted earnings of $44.00 to $46.00 a share in the fiscal first quarter, a smaller step up than the last quarter's jump from $23.41 to $39.25.

Management's own long-term plan is more modest still. For fiscal 2028 through 2030, it assumes revenue grows in the mid-to-high teens, with gross margin near 80%, below the 84.6% it just reported. In other words, Sandisk is not planning on prices that keep climbing. Investors who want more on stocks the market is wary of can see our ranking of 10 Stocks Investors Are Running Away From .

Story Continues

What the Low Multiple Assumes

The forward price-to-earnings ratio is about 6, based on estimated adjusted earnings for fiscal 2027, against a sector median of about 21. Consensus estimates call for earnings per share to grow about 203% in fiscal 2027, so the stock looks cheap on the year now under way. That gap fits a market treating this year as peak earnings. Sandisk has traded on its own only since February 2025, so there is no five-year average to compare it with. For investors looking to add more chip exposure, our list of 12 Best Performing Semiconductor Stocks to Invest In is worth a look.

Anyone who owns the stock is effectively betting that the contracts and datacenter demand turn out better than the market fears. Sandisk also has $15.5 billion left on its buyback authorization and says it plans to return all excess cash to shareholders after investing in the business.

The market looks to be pricing a peak already, and for the next two years the contracts and guidance don't point that way. The years after that are where Sandisk's own plan flattens growth, so they are the harder part to price. The report due at the end of this month will show whether gross margin stays within the guided range of 83.0% to 85.0%. That would be the clearest sign that prices are staying firm.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SNDK as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Title: Sandisk (SNDK)  vs. Texas Instruments (TXN): How Much Cash-Yield Protection Does Memory Offer?
news.Content:
Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade includes both memory and analog exposure. Sandisk's strong cash generation creates an apparent valuation advantage over Texas Instruments. The useful question is how much that cash can decline before the advantage disappears, rather than assuming today's memory economics last a decade. Sandisk Corporation (NASDAQ: SNDK ) sells NAND-based storage products. Texas Instruments Incorporated (NASDAQ: TXN ) supplies analog and embedded chips across many applications. These are alternative semiconductor portfolio exposures, not direct product competitors.

Reconcile the cash before comparing the price

Sandisk's fiscal 2026 operating cash was $11.671 billion. Deduct $177 million of direct capital spending and $275 million of net manufacturing-joint-venture funding, and $11.219 billion remains. Removing a further $2.591 billion increase in refund and contract liabilities leaves $8.628 billion for this diagnostic comparison.

That last adjustment tests cash supported by customer funding. It is not a full estimate of normal earnings, and it differs from the company's $8.743 billion adjusted free-cash-flow measure because the liability adjustment is broader. Other working-capital and tax effects remain.

Texas Instruments generated $8.667 billion of operating cash over the twelve months through June. Deducting $3.312 billion of capital spending leaves $5.355 billion before separate capital-incentive proceeds. Operating cash still includes $433 million of investment-tax-credit benefits, so this is not a fully subsidy-free measure.

A large gap can still be cyclical

Against October 16 equity values of $190.24 billion and $252.49 billion, the resulting cash yields are 4.5% for Sandisk and 2.1% for Texas Instruments. Sandisk's adjusted residual could fall about 53% before matching Texas Instruments' current yield, if prices and the latter's cash stayed fixed.

That is a break-even calculation, not a downside limit. With a 60% decline in Sandisk's residual, its yield would fall to about 1.8%, below the analog company's starting yield. Our Sandisk business analysis examines the demand and pricing conditions behind today's profits.

Texas Instruments offers long-lived products and broader applications, but its factories also need utilization. New capacity can depress cash returns before demand catches up, and a large dividend leaves less room to retain cash. Sandisk's joint ventures share manufacturing investment while preserving fixed-cost and funding obligations. Our Micron cash-reserve analysis explains why memory investors should examine commitments alongside liquidity.

Story Continues

Sandisk's August investor day supplied a counterargument: eight customer agreements carry committed volumes, minimum financial guarantees and structured pricing. Management expects them to cover about half of fiscal 2027 bits. Those contracts may reduce old-cycle volatility, although their performance through a downturn remains unproven.

What would change the decision?

A dividend is not an independent source of protection.

Q2 2026 hedge-fund holders rose to 128 from 114 for Sandisk and to 111 from 71 for Texas Instruments. Fundsmith reduced Texas Instruments shares 32%. Texas Instruments' September 30 short interest was 2.25% of float.

Sandisk offers the larger starting cash yield even after these adjustments. Texas Instruments offers a different product-cycle exposure, not immunity from cyclicality. The calculated 53% cushion is useful only while the analog cash baseline holds. Investors should require evidence that storage pricing and customer commitments sustain cash generation before interpreting the gap as lasting undervaluation.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SNDK and TXN as investments, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Title: Micron vs. Lam Research: Does Buying the Tool Supplier Reduce Memory-Cycle Risk?
news.Content: Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MU ) generated $89.68 billion of operating cash in its fiscal year ended September 3. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX ) generated $5.86 billion in its year ended June 28. The relevant question is what remains after investment when those collections weaken. Micron and Lam Research offer different ways to invest in memory demand within our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade . Micron sells memory; Lam supplies manufacturing tools and support. Buying the supplier changes the timing and mechanism of exposure, but it does not escape customers' investment cycles. Source: Micron Technology Owning production creates a larger commitment Micron spent $30.71 billion on property, plant and equipment before government incentives. Lam spent $966 million on capital expenditure and intangible assets. Those investments consumed about 34% and 16% of operating cash, respectively. Hold those investment bills fixed and reduce operating cash 50%. Micron would retain about $14.13 billion after investment; Lam would retain $1.96 billion. Relative to their respective annual revenue, those residuals equal 10.6% and 8.4%. The larger factory bill does not automatically leave Micron with the weaker current cushion because its starting cash generation is exceptionally high. Micron's memory prices can change quickly; Lam's equipment orders can respond later and fall sharply when customers postpone capacity. Our Micron liquidity analysis examines why a strong cash balance still needs to be compared with future obligations. The supplier has more than one source of demand Lam also serves advanced logic manufacturing, while its support business includes service, spares, upgrades and older-generation tools. That gives it exposure beyond a single memory maker's output. It does not turn the company into a subscription business or guarantee that service collections stay flat during lower factory utilization. Micron's technology and product mix could sustain stronger economics than older memory cycles suggest. The bear case is that competitive supply eventually catches up with demand, reducing prices while substantial investment continues. The price already distinguishes the two At October 16 equity values, Micron cost about 17 times annual cash after gross capital spending, versus about 68 times for Lam. If Micron's cash after investment fell 75%, its multiple would rise to about 67 at an unchanged share price. That illustrates how much exceptional memory profitability supports the apparent discount; it does not establish that a 75% decline is likely or that equal multiples imply equal value. Story Continues Lam's flexibility also depends on capital allocation. Our Lam-Applied payout comparison shows how annual repurchases and dividends can exceed cash left after investment. Q2 2026 hedge-fund holders rose to 184 from 154 for Micron and to 139 from 123 for Lam. AQR reduced Micron shares 16%, and Arrowstreet reduced Lam shares 7%. Micron's September 30 short interest was 2.31% of float. Lam reduces direct exposure to memory selling prices and owned-fab spending. Micron starts with a stronger cash yield and a large current funding cushion. The choice depends on confidence in memory economics versus equipment demand; neither company's latest cash flow should be treated as a permanent floor. While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MU and LRCX as investments, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Lam Research ( NASDAQ:LRCX ) shares rose about 4% Monday as investors looked ahead to fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings and Deutsche Bank raised its price target on the semiconductor-equipment company.

Expectations for semiconductor equipment are already high.

The bigger upside would come from proving that Lam can capture more share, defend margins and potentially exercise additional pricing power as DRAM and advanced logic investment accelerates.

That could differentiate the company even if the entire semiconductor-capital-equipment group benefits from the same spending cycle.

For investors, the key things to watch Wednesday are gross-margin guidance, DRAM exposure, foundry-logic orders, new-node share gains and management's commentary on 2027 and 2028 wafer-fab spending .

Micron's fiscal year ended September 3 produced $89.675 billion of operating cash against $30.712 billion of property, plant and equipment purchases, leaving $58.963 billion. Its higher reported adjusted free cash flow includes government incentives, so the gross-spending calculation better isolates the investment burden before that support.

Sandisk's year ended July 3 generated $11.671 billion of operating cash and only $177 million of direct capital expenditure. But it also advanced $462 million to manufacturing ventures and received $187 million of loan repayments. Subtracting that $275 million net funding, alongside direct spending, leaves $11.219 billion.

The ventures also sell wafers to Sandisk. Those purchases already affect operating cash and must not be deducted again. The annual report describes obligations to fund roughly half of venture investment when internal resources are insufficient, and to bear half of fixed costs even when production falls. Partnership changes where the bill appears; it does not eliminate manufacturing exposure.

Customer cash can flatter the comparison

Sandisk's operating cash included increases of $1.374 billion in refund liabilities and $1.217 billion in contract liabilities. Removing those two contributions from the $11.219 billion residual leaves $8.628 billion. Sandisk reports $8.743 billion of adjusted free cash flow using a narrower $2.476 billion adjustment for its new business model's prepayments and deposits. Our broader liability adjustment is not normalized cash flow; taxes, inventories and other working capital are still of importance.

Micron classified $12.747 billion of customer contract deposits in financing cash flow. Those deposits therefore are not inside the operating-cash starting point and should not be subtracted from it again. Refundability still matters when assessing how much of Micron's cash can protect investors in a downturn .

Story Continues

Using October 16 market capitalizations of $994.34 billion and $190.24 billion, Micron trades at 16.9 times its gross-spending cash residual. Sandisk is at 17.0 times after net venture funding, rising to 22.0 times after removing those liability inflows. These historical cash diagnostics show why choosing a denominator can change an apparent bargain.

Micron's broader DRAM and NAND exposure supports its investment case, but owning factories means paying for capacity before future demand is certain. Sandisk's shared manufacturing structure can reduce direct investment needs, though fixed-cost commitments remain when NAND pricing weakens. Its growing enterprise business also cannot make every dollar equally durable; see how much of Sandisk's profit boom data centers can sustain .

Q2 2026 hedge-fund participation in Insider Monkey's database increased to 184 from 154 for Micron and to 128 from 114 for Sandisk. AQR's reported Micron shares fell 16% to 3.83 million over that quarter. Micron's September 30 short interest was 26,023,190 shares, 2.31% of float and 1.06 days to cover.

Sandisk still spent less through direct capital expenditure and net venture loans relative to revenue. The stronger investment conclusion requires recurring cash after customer advances and manufacturing commitments, not that capital-spending line alone. Our Micron-Sandisk investment comparison examines the separate product-mix and valuation choice.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MU and SNDK as investments, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. news.Title: ASML vs. Lam Research: How Much Protection Does Service Revenue Really Provide?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ: ASML ) reported about €3.3 billion of installed-base management sales in its September quarter. Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ: LRCX ) reported $2.47 billion of customer-support-related revenue and other in its June quarter. The labels describe different mixtures. ASML and Lam Research both feature in our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade . Both have large businesses supporting equipment already inside chip factories. That can soften a new-equipment slowdown, but calling all of that revenue recurring would give investors too much confidence.

Image: Courtesy of ASML

Start with what each category includes

ASML defines installed-base management as net service and field-option sales. Its customers need to maintain costly lithography machines, while upgrades can improve their productivity. Yet upgrades remain spending decisions; the entire category should not be treated as an annually contracted subscription.

Lam's category combines service, spares, upgrades and non-leading-edge Reliant equipment. That last component is equipment sales. The reported support share therefore cannot establish how much purely recurring service revenue Lam has.

Using rounded ASML figures, installed-base sales represented about 28% of quarterly revenue. Lam's broader category represented 36.8%.

Stress the revenue mix, not an invented subscription base

Assume new-system revenue falls 20% while each support category stays flat. ASML's total sales would decline about 14.4%; Lam's would decline 12.6%. If support revenue also falls 10%, the declines become about 17.2% and 16.3%.

Lam's reported mix produces the smaller decline in this exercise, but its equipment content makes a flat support assumption less secure. Neither company discloses enough here to calculate a directly comparable service-only cushion. Lower factory utilization can also reduce demand for spares and usage-related work.

Technology leadership still needs a sensible price

ASML benefits from advanced lithography transitions; Lam benefits from increasingly complex deposition and etch processes. Both face export restrictions and delayed customer investments. Our TSMC-ASML cash comparison explains why a strong cash quarter can also reflect payment timing rather than a permanently larger earnings base.

At October 16 equity values, trailing cash after capital expenditure cost about 26 times for ASML and 68 times for Lam. Working-capital movements make those historical multiples imperfect measures of sustainable cash; the service-mix exercise cannot justify a stock-price target.

Story Continues

Export rules can affect both systems and support. Our ASML geographic-risk analysis explains why a wider customer footprint is not complete protection.

Q2 2026 hedge-fund holders rose to 140 from 133 for ASML and to 139 from 123 for Lam. Fisher increased ASML shares 3%, while Arrowstreet reduced Lam shares 7%. ASML's September 30 short interest was 0.37% of float.

Both installed bases provide business opportunities beyond new-tool shipments. Investors should favor evidence of resilient service collections and profitable upgrades over the largest reported support percentage. Lam's broader category offers a useful buffer, but the disclosures do not establish that it has the stronger recurring-revenue franchise.

While we acknowledge the potential of ASML and LRCX as investments, we believe certain other AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lumentum Holdings Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

AI infrastructure stocks are selling off even as suppliers report sold-out capacity, rising guidance and multi-year backlogs, according to TradeSmith's Lucas Downey.

Lumentum, Dell Technologies and Everpure each show falling share prices alongside rising earnings estimates, compressing forward valuations and creating a widening gap between price and fundamentals.

Downey views the decline as driven by investor positioning and seasonal weakness rather than broken fundamentals, and says upcoming earnings revisions will determine when the sell-off ends.

The artificial intelligence (AI) trade finally cracked. After months of resilience while utilities, real estate and consumer discretionary names took a beating, the market's favorite growth story is now the one getting sold, and investors sitting on big gains are rushing to lock them in.

The fear has a familiar shape. Earlier this year, software stocks were written off as AI roadkill, and the slide dragged on for roughly 60 days. Many of those same names have since reclaimed all-time highs, because the earnings never broke the way the headlines said they would.

→ These 3 Green Stocks Have a Growth Story That Goes Far Beyond Washington

That's the tension now. Prices are falling across AI infrastructure while the companies building it keep raising guidance, reporting sold-out capacity and pointing to backlogs that stretch for years. When price and fundamentals move in opposite directions, valuations compress, and that gap is where opportunity tends to surface.

AI Sell-Off Looks Driven by Positioning, Not Broken Fundamentals

The selling looks more like positioning than a verdict on the businesses, per Lucas Downey, editor at TradeSmith. Many investors came into the slide underweight in the interest-rate-sensitive stocks that look most attractive as rates come down, while sitting on large embedded gains in AI. Selling the winners is the fastest way to rebalance, while some heavily leveraged investors may have no choice but to sell.

→ The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway

Seasonality adds friction. Late September has historically been weak, and midterm election years tend to run volatile as investors handicap the fight for Congress. Downey sees signs of capitulation and puts a potential bottom in the next couple of weeks, with earnings season the likely catalyst. By his read, further downside remains on the table.

Story Continues

The deeper worry, though, is whether hyperscalers can keep paying for the build-out as data center costs climb. Downey points to what suppliers are reporting. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) and ASML Holding (NASDAQ: ASML) have described demand as strong and, in many cases, accelerating, and committed contracts stretch out for years.

→ Tesla's Roadster Reveal Hints at 2 Much Bigger Moves

Optical Components Sell Out Into 2029 as Earnings Estimates Rise

Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) makes the lasers and optical components that move enormous volumes of data at high speed inside AI data centers. As demand runs into the limits of materials and manufacturing capacity, those parts become a bottleneck.

CEO Michael Hurlston has said the company is sold out of optical components for AI servers through early 2029. Sales over the last 12 months came in just over $3 billion, and estimates cited by Downey call for about $6.3 billion over the next 12 months, approaching $10 billion the year after. Earnings per share (EPS) estimates sit at $21.70 for fiscal 2027 and $47.88 for fiscal 2029.

A roughly 400% gain over the past year is exactly what makes latecomers nervous. But the stock has dropped about 15% in a week, and with estimates rising as the price falls, the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio has compressed to about 42. The market is pricing a momentum unwind. Another round of upward estimate revisions could change that, so earnings follow-through is the thing to watch.

AI Server Demand Fuels a Blowout Beat and Raise

Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) spent decades as the personal computer brand everyone knew. Its infrastructure business, spanning servers, storage, networking equipment and software, has turned it into a cornerstone of the AI build-out, and the stock has climbed more than 200% in a year.

The latest quarter was a beat and a raise. Per Downey, Dell guided third-quarter EPS to $6.50 against estimates of $4.46 and revenue to $49 billion against a consensus just above $41 billion, then lifted its fiscal 2027 outlook. In his view, the stock effectively repriced on that report.

A surprise that big raises the bar, and priced-for-perfection risk is real. The counterweight is valuation. With forward estimates climbing while shares slide, the forward P/E has fallen to around 18, below the broader market. The market is pricing an AI hardware hangover. Next quarter's results are what to watch, since they test whether this guidance was a one-off.

Enterprise Flash Storage Lands Hyperscale Wins and a Higher Outlook

The smallest of the three is Everpure (NYSE: P), which builds all-flash data storage systems, the infrastructure companies use to manage data and run AI workloads, at enterprise scale. Management had flagged hyperscale customer wins, and those are starting to show up in results.

Everpure reiterated guidance and raised its preliminary fiscal 2028 outlook to $7.15 billion at the midpoint, against a Street estimate of $6.2 billion. That's a message of acceleration, not slowdown. The stock also scores an 88 on TradeSmith's proprietary Quantum Edge system, which blends fundamental and technical factors into a single rating; TradeSmith reads that as a high-quality stock.

Storage and memory names such as Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) have been caught in the same downdraft, even as workloads keep growing. A smaller company brings bigger swings, and stocks don't move in straight lines. What could change sentiment is continued upward movement in analysts' EPS forecasts, and that trend is the one to watch.

Earnings Revisions Hold the Key to the End of the AI Sell-Off

Lumentum, Dell and Everpure sit at different links in the same chain: optics that move the data, servers that process it and storage that holds it. What connects them is a widening gap—falling share prices against rising forward numbers.

The risk is that the hyperscaler spending debate drags on, flows stay negative, and the smaller names take the hardest hits, much like software's two-month grind. The upside is that sold-out capacity, multi-year backlogs and raised guidance are company-reported numbers, and compressed valuations leave room to recover if earnings season confirms them.

None of this requires calling the exact bottom. It does require hyperscalers to keep spending and these companies to deliver on guidance already issued. Stay focused on earnings revisions, because that's what moves these stocks once the selling runs its course.

news.Title: Oracle Slumped 9% Amid a Tech Selloff and AI Buildout Concerns. Investors Should Cautiously Buy the Dip.
news.Content:
Oracle's (ORCL) artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions come with a hefty price tag, and investors are now questioning how much risk they should accept to fund it. Shares tumbled nearly 9% in a single session on Oct. 14 as a broader technology selloff put the financing of AI infrastructure under scrutiny.

The pressure extended across the sector. CoreWeave (CRWV) dropped more than 15% as a selloff in its corporate bonds heightened financing concerns, while Marvell Technology (MRVL) lost more than 8%.

More News from Barchart

Intel vs. AMD: The CPU Comeback Has Become a 2-Stock Fight, But 1 Is the Better Buy

Micron Stock Alert: Elon Musk Just Made The Bull Case Even Stronger

No 'Example Anywhere on the Planet': Billionaire Kevin O'Leary's Utah Data Center Could Use Enough Electricity to Power 16 Million People

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Hotter-than-expected inflation data added further pressure. U.S. annual inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August, raising the prospect of higher interest rates and more expensive financing for the industry's massive infrastructure buildout.

For Oracle, this strikes at the core of its investment case. The sharp selloff, therefore, raises a more fundamental question. Has the decline created an attractive opportunity to invest in the AI expansion? Or is the lower share price a warning of the financial risks? Let's find out.

Oracle's Financial Check

Based in Austin, Texas, Oracle is valued at approximately $387 billion by market capitalization and provides enterprise databases, business applications, and cloud infrastructure for organizations managing data and deploying AI. Beyond its established software business, the company is expanding computing capacity to serve customers requiring infrastructure for demanding AI workloads.

ORCL stock closed on Oct. 16 at $128.23 per share. The stock has declined 33% year-to-date (YTD) and 55% for the past 52 weeks.

At 19.7 times trailing earnings versus the roughly 32 times sector median, Oracle looks cheaper on earnings but pricier on sales at 6 times versus about 3.5 times for the sector. Oracle's $2 annualized dividend also yields approximately 1.49%.

Oracle released first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Sept. 10. Revenue rose 30% year-over-year (YOY) to $19.35 billion, beating the $19.1 billion analyst estimate. Adjusted EPS also increased 30% YOY to $1.92 and exceeded the $1.74 consensus estimate.

Story Continues

That earnings strength extended to operating results. Oracle reported adjusted operating income of $8.15 billion against expectations of $7.8 billion. This was a 4.5% beat, with an adjusted operating margin of roughly 42%.

Cloud infrastructure drove much of the revenue growth, jumping 121% to $7.4 billion. Cloud applications revenue increased 10% to $4.2 billion, while software revenue fell 3% to $5.5 billion.

To support that cloud expansion, the company delivered 850 megawatts of additional data-center capacity and more than 300,000 GPUs. Those GPU deliveries nearly tripled the preceding quarter's total.

Oracle also added more than $30 billion in AI cloud contracts during the quarter. This pushed remaining performance obligations (RPO) to $664 billion, up $209 billion YOY.

However, the expansion continued to weigh on cash flow. Free cash flow fell to -$5.4 billion from -$1.87 billion in the previous quarter.

Oracle's Next Growth Drivers

Oracle's latest product launches and partnerships show where its next phase of growth could come from and what shareholders will help finance. On Sept. 29, Oracle introduced Fusion Claw with 25 new applications, expanding its agentic application portfolio to 75. The technology combines AI reasoning with precise enterprise computation to automate complex tasks under customer-defined controls.

Infrastructure security is advancing, too. On Oct. 13, Oracle, Microsoft (MSFT), and Marvell established an Open Compute Project working group targeting NIST FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security. Their proposed server-integrated security module would protect cryptographic keys where workloads run, reducing network dependence and supporting regulatory compliance.

Oracle also launched Nexus Case Flow and Nexus Reach on Sept. 29 for financial crime investigations. These offerings target compliance workloads where efficiency must coexist with accountability.

That same day, NetApp (NTAP) and Oracle announced OCI NetApp Storage Service, with general availability planned within 12 months. Its ONTAP capabilities would help customers migrate databases, enterprise applications, and AI workloads without substantially redesigning existing storage operations.

However, expansion brings obligations beyond hardware. On Oct. 2, Oracle committed to absorbing approximately $300 million in rising Point Beach nuclear energy costs, benefiting over 1 million Wisconsin utility customers. The company's related Project Lighthouse development projects more than $11 billion in local economic benefits, 4,000 construction jobs over three years, and 1,000 ongoing positions.

These initiatives give Oracle more ways to win cloud business, but they also add to the spending shareholders must weigh. The key is how quickly those commitments translate into revenue and stronger cash flow.

Wall Street's Case for Oracle

Oracle's next earnings report is scheduled for Dec. 9. Analysts expect November-quarter EPS of $1.57, down 19% from $1.95 a year earlier.

Despite that projected decline, Citi sees an opportunity. In August, the firm placed Oracle on a 90-day upside catalyst watch, maintaining a "Buy" rating and a $330 price target. Citi's thesis rests on AI infrastructure demand supporting stronger cloud growth, pricing, and profitability. Citi also identified earnings and an upcoming investor day as potential catalysts.

JPMorgan offered a more measured endorsement in August, retaining an "Overweight" rating while cutting its target to $200 from $210. Analyst Samik Chatterjee noted aggressive infrastructure spending and capital requirements but maintained that Oracle could capitalize on AI expansion.

That optimism extends beyond Citi and JPMorgan. Across 43 analysts with coverage, ORCL stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating. The average price target of $242.22 implies potential upside of approximately 86% from current levels.

Conclusion

Oracle looks more like a cautious buy than a stock to avoid. Strong cloud growth supports the opportunity, but heavy spending and negative free cash flow warrant smaller positions rather than aggressive buying. A gradual recovery looks more likely than a quick rebound, provided demand holds and financing remains manageable. The next earnings report will need to show that expansion is producing better financial results. Buying shares gradually makes sense here, but chasing a bounce before cash flow improves would be premature.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Shot Higher Today
news.Content:
Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) charged sharply higher on Monday, jumping as much as 8.3%. As of 11:24 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 7.9%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

While a rebound in technology issues certainly helped, the semiconductor specialist rallied on positive news in the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) space.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Industry standard

Earlier this year, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced the development of NVHBM, the company's custom HBM architecture. NVHBM is a custom HBM die that delivers 15% lower power consumption and 30% higher bandwidth, all on a smaller die than HBM4e. To be clear, this isn't a replacement for traditional HBM, but rather connective technology between Nvidia's NVLink and HBM chips.

A report emerged over the weekend that Nvidia has asked Samsung Electronics to adopt Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing 's 3-nanometer chipmaking process to produce the NVHBM dies, according to a story that first appeared in the Seoul Economic Daily. This will mark the first such collaboration between TSMC and Samsung, according to the report.

Moreover, Nvidia has approached the industry's biggest memory producers, including Micron Technology and SK Hynix , to use this process, which would standardize it across multiple memory suppliers. This, in turn, would free up valuable real estate on the compute die, resulting in up to 30% additional compute.

Investors have been concerned that demand for artificial intelligence (AI) could falter, thereby reducing demand for the AI chips. This move by Nvidia suggests that -- despite fears to the contrary -- the adoption of AI still has room to run. This suggests that the same is true for memory chip suppliers.

Even in the face of unprecedented demand for memory chips, Sandisk stock is selling for just 19 times earnings and 6 times forward earnings. This gives investors the opportunity to pick up shares at a discount.

news.Title: If Apple Cuts iPhone Units in 2027, This Stock Could Be a Big Loser
news.Content:
Apple (AAPL) is reportedly asking several key suppliers to scale back component production for its flagship devices, as higher retail prices driven by rising memory chip costs appear to be cooling consumer demand. And if iPhone sales lose steam, the ripple effects could reach far beyond Apple itself.

Take Cirrus Logic (CRUS), for instance. The semiconductor company relies heavily on Apple, which contributes the lion's share of its revenue, according to KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh. With Apple reportedly taking a more cautious approach to iPhone production, Vinh sees a risk that unit sales could stay flat or slip slightly in 2027, dampening Cirrus Logic's growth prospects. That concern prompted him to downgrade CRUS stock, adding to the pressure on shares.

More News from Barchart

Intel vs. AMD: The CPU Comeback Has Become a 2-Stock Fight, But 1 Is the Better Buy

Micron Stock Alert: Elon Musk Just Made The Bull Case Even Stronger

What a New Nvidia-Backed AI Platform Means for Honeywell Stock

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Cirrus supplies custom audio and mixed-signal chips used in smartphones, making it particularly sensitive to changes in Apple's production plans. With its potential PC growth opportunity also facing delays, investors have more than one reason to pay attention. So, if Apple trims iPhone production in 2027, could Cirrus Logic be among the biggest losers? Let's take a closer look.

About Cirrus Logic Stock

Founded in 1984, Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia. The company designs high-performance analog, mixed-signal, and audio digital signal processing (DSP) integrated circuits used in smartphones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches, automotive entertainment systems, and other consumer electronics.

Its product portfolio includes smart codecs, amplifiers, haptics and sensing solutions, camera controllers, and battery and power ICs. With approximately 1,717 employees worldwide, Cirrus Logic focuses on power efficiency, audio quality, and innovative chip designs. The company has a market capitalization of around $5.4 billion.

Cirrus Logic's stock started the year on a high note, climbing to $180.42 in May 2026 as strong fiscal 2026 results and optimism around the semiconductor sector gave investors plenty to cheer about. But that enthusiasm has since faded. By Oct. 15, shares had tumbled to a 52-week low of $105.10, down 40% from their peak. CRUS stock has lost 14% over the past year and 35% over six months, with recent losses reflecting softer PC market expectations and concerns about its heavy reliance on Apple, its largest customer.

Story Continues

Things got more interesting after Cirrus announced its acquisition of Italy-based INVENTVM Semiconductor on Oct. 6. The deal aims to expand its technology portfolio and reach new markets, but the financial terms remain undisclosed, and management expects no material revenue impact. That may explain why investors have not warmed up to the deal just yet, as they weigh its long-term potential against the lack of an immediate financial boost.

Technically, CRUS stock shows signs of stabilization, but the picture remains shaky. The 14-day RSI has bounced back from oversold territory to around 34, though it is still below the neutral mark. Meanwhile, the MACD line remains below its signal line, with a negative histogram pointing to continued bearish momentum.

On the valuation front, CRUS stock looks relatively affordable, trading at 12.88 times forward adjusted earnings and 2.68 times forward sales. Both multiples sit below the stock's five-year averages and those of its sector peers, making its current valuation worth a closer look.

A Closer Look at Cirrus Logic's Q1 Earnings Report

In August, Cirrus Logic released its Q1 2027 earnings report and started the year on a strong note, posting record first-quarter revenue and earnings. That's largely due to healthy demand for custom chips used in premium smartphones. The company also made progress on its broader growth plans, although its PC business faced a few speed bumps.

Revenue rose 12.9% year-over-year (YoY) to $460 million, almost in line with Wall Street's expectations. Sales also increased 2.5% sequentially as stronger shipments of smartphone components lifted results. Demand for custom-boosted amplifiers and smart codecs remained strong, helping the company deliver record quarterly earnings. Adjusted EPS climbed 21.9% annually to $1.84, beating analysts' estimates. However, previously anticipated pricing reductions partly offset the revenue gains. Cirrus remains heavily reliant on its biggest customer, Apple, which accounted for 90% of first-quarter revenue.

Beyond smartphones, Cirrus is working to expand its footprint in AI-enabled PCs and other markets. Interest in its latest low-power smart codec for AI PCs remains strong, with multiple customers working on designs expected to launch next calendar year. However, supply constraints involving a key industry platform, memory and other components, along with delayed PC launches, have pushed expected growth further out.

As a result, management lowered its fiscal 2027 PC revenue expectations, describing the challenges as timing issues rather than a change in the long-term opportunity. Several customers have also announced PCs based on Nvidia's (NVDA) RTX Spark platform that are expected to ship later this year with Cirrus amplifiers and codecs.

The company is also advancing its next-generation camera controller and smart power IC for 3D sensing, while a newly taped-out high-performance analog front-end component targeting metrology applications adds to its general market portfolio.

Cirrus ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and investments and no debt. Operating cash flow reached $64.1 million, while free cash flow came in at $48.6 million, representing an 11% margin. The company repurchased about 211,000 shares for $34.5 million during the quarter and bought another 359,000 shares for $50.5 million after quarter-end. Management continues to prioritize investments in the business, followed by acquisitions and share buybacks, with no near-term dividend planned.

Looking ahead, Cirrus expects Q2 revenue between $510 million and $570 million, with the midpoint implying 17% sequential growth but roughly 4% YoY decline. GAAP gross margin is projected at 52% to 54%. While smartphone demand remains a key support, investors will be watching whether Cirrus can turn its growing AI-PC pipeline into meaningful revenue as supply constraints ease.

Cirrus Logic is gearing up to report its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the closing bell, and Wall Street will be watching to see how the chipmaker is holding up. Analysts expect revenue to come in at around $540.4 million, while EPS is projected to slip nearly 16% YoY to $2.11. Looking further ahead, fiscal 2027 earnings are expected to fall 8.9% annually to $7.24 per share. There could be some relief in fiscal 2028, though, with EPS projected to rebound 4.7% YoY to $7.58.

What Do Analysts Think About CRUS Stock?

KeyBanc downgraded CRUS stock to a "Sector Weight" from an "Overweight," citing its heavy reliance on Apple and delayed diversification prospects. Analyst John Vinh noted that Apple's cuts to TSMC (TSM) wafer starts, equivalent to 15 million to 20 million iPhones, suggest weaker iPhone volumes in 2027.

With roughly 90% of Cirrus Logic's revenue tied to Apple, Vinh sees limited growth over the next six to 12 months. Meanwhile, elevated memory prices and an expected 10% to 15% decline in PC shipments this year could delay its PC diversification plans, despite meaningful share gains in the segment. KeyBanc also questioned Cirrus' unsuccessful Synaptics (SYNA) acquisition bid from a strategic standpoint.

Analysts have been moderately bullish about Cirrus Logic, with seven who cover the stock giving a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Among them, three suggest a "Strong Buy," three are playing it safe with a "Hold" rating, while the remaining one has a "Strong Sell."

The mean price target of $123.20 indicates CRUS has an upside potential of 13%, and the high target of $200 suggests that the stock could rise as much as 83% from the current price level.

news.Title: Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) Upgraded to Strong Buy: Here's What You Should Know
news.Content:
Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) could be a solid addition to your portfolio given its recent upgrade to a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). This upgrade primarily reflects an upward trend in earnings estimates, which is one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.

The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.

Individual investors often find it hard to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, since these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time. In these situations, the Zacks rating system comes in handy because of the power of a changing earnings picture in determining near-term stock price movements.

Therefore, the Zacks rating upgrade for Sandisk Corporation basically reflects positivity about its earnings outlook that could translate into buying pressure and an increase in its stock price.

Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices

The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated.
